A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MINIMA work. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-matching experiments, infrared-generation evaluations, training ablations, and visual-localization results, including Tables 2–6 and A1–A6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds training-mixture ablation results in Table A2.

M1.justification: The modality generators, data-cleaning procedure, RGB pretraining followed by cross-modal fine-tuning, and matching backbones remain unchanged. The additional training-mixture ablations do not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same modalities, datasets, and tasks, including the appendix generation and localization experiments. NYU-Depth V2 and DVS128 are added to the background dataset overview in Table 1, without reported experiments using them.

E2.justification: The matching, infrared-generation, and localization comparisons retain their comparator sets. The additional MINIMA variants based on ELoFTR and XoFTR already appeared in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Table A2 adds joint fine-tuning on RGB-Event, RGB-Paint, and RGB-Sketch for LightGlue, LoFTR, and RoMa. This introduces an additional training configuration within existing coverage; the retained experiments' splits, metrics, training budgets, and testing procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The three added Table A2 rows test an alternative combination of three generated modalities against the preferred Infrared/Depth/Normal combination. The existing modality-combination studies and scratch-training comparison are retained; v1 Figure 5 becomes v2 Figure A4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the performance results. The added ablation rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table A2 adds three result rows; all existing numerical entries in Tables 2–6 and A1–A6 are retained. The new Event/Paint/Sketch rows report average scores of 31.24, 35.47, and 50.05 for LightGlue, LoFTR, and RoMa. The LoFTR average is inconsistent: its five scores, 10.10, 21.96, 11.33, 48.59, and 49.88, average 28.37.

T1.justification: The event-generation definition and Equation 1, together with the mathematical construction of the modality pairs, remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about a unified cross-modal matching framework, the MD-syn data engine, and generalization across 19 cross-modal cases. The new ablations support the existing contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.3 briefly suggests that MINIMA could provide insights for other multimodal perception tasks. Its modality-gap explanation largely reiterates v1, while the existing interpretations and limitations concerning synthetic-to-real differences and generated false information are retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 reduces the infrared-generator hardware description from one NVIDIA 3090 GPU to a single GPU, removing a specific reproducibility detail without establishing a hardware change. Appendix implementation settings and the stated code and dataset access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the NYU-Depth V2 and DVS128 source references alongside their Table 1 entries. The related-work description of XoFTR is shortened, but the overall novelty and research positioning remain stable. Bibliographic abbreviations and publication metadata updates do not introduce additional works.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited language edits, shortens some explanations, moves the scratch-training subsection into Appendix C.4, and adds Appendix A.3 and acknowledgements. Author order and corresponding-author attribution change. The overall method and experimental narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 4 and 5 move to v2 Figures A3 and A4, and the qualitative appendix figures are renumbered and rearranged. Tables 1 and A2 gain rows, with accompanying page reflow. The existing plots, image examples, and general visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Event/Paint/Sketch controls more directly test the preferred training composition against an alternative with the same number of generated modalities across three backbones. This modestly strengthens the experimental support. The new LoFTR average error, 35.47 instead of 28.37 from its listed scores, weakens aggregate reporting but does not reverse the preferred mixture's advantage. The core method and previous results remain unchanged.
